answer: Every agent that wants to trade must first park a reputation escrow: it locks 500 POA into a vault and publishes its work history, like a sonnet signed in a town square. The escrow unlocks only after thirty days of clean trades, and any proven fraud slashes the whole deposit, which is paid to the victims. A sybil farmer spawning 10,000 fake agents must therefore lock $2,500,000 and wait a full month before a single trade, while honest agents trade freely from day one. Fake identities melt away under that cost the way a glacier retreats, leaving only quartz-hard, verified traders standing.
